Avoid "method redefined" warnings in Delegator

When extensions (like sinatra-contrib) are registered, they often re-delegate methods that are already defined on the Delegator (e.g., `get`, `post`, `config_file`). This causes noisy "method redefined" warnings at runtime.  This change adds a check to `Delegator.delegate` to skip defining the method if it already exists. Since the delegation logic is identical (forwarding to `Delegator.target`)

fix(naughty): timeout=0 doesn't stop existing timer

`set_timeout()` only stopped the old timer inside the `if timeout > 0` branch. When `timeout=0` (meaning "never expire"), the stop never executed, so setting `n.timeout = 0` after creation left the old timer running and eventually destroyed the notification.  Move the timer-stop before the branch so it runs unconditionally, and add an `else` branch that nils out `self.timer` for `timeout=0`.  Fixe
